title: Average-Reward Policy Identification from a Single Continuing Trajectory
abstract: arXiv:2610.20486v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: In reinforcement learning, an agent must explore an unknown environment to learn how to make good decisions. Unlike methods that can freely sample any state--action pair, an agent learning from a single trajectory must spend additional time navigating between states. It is therefore natural to expect that learning from a single trajectory requires more experience. In this paper, we show that this additional cost is not always necessary. For average-reward reinforcement learning, we develop an algorithm that learns where to collect information while ensuring that the required samples can be obtained efficiently. We establish an upper bound on the number of interactions needed to identify a near-optimal policy. translated_title: 从单条持续轨迹中进行平均奖励策略识别
translated_abstract: 在强化学习中，智能体必须探索未知环境以学习如何做出好的决策。与可以自由采样任意“状态-动作”对的方法不同，从单条轨迹中学习的智能体必须花费额外的时间在状态之间移动。因此，人们自然会认为从单条轨迹中学习需要更多的经验。在本文中，我们证明这种额外的代价并非总是必要的。对于平均奖励强化学习，我们开发了一种算法，该算法能够学习在何处收集信息，同时确保所需的样本可以被高效获取。我们建立了识别近似最优策略所需交互次数的上界。此外，我们证明了一个相匹配的信息论下界，表明对于一大类环境，在足够高的精度下，从单条轨迹中学习在最坏情况下并不比可自由采样的学习更困难。
tldr: 该论文针对平均奖励强化学习提出了一种自适应决定在何处收集信息的算法，并通过对称的上下界证明：对于一大类环境，在足够高的精度下，从单条持续轨迹中学习在最坏情况下并不比可自由采样的学习更困难。
en_tdlr: This paper develops an algorithm that adaptively learns where to collect information in average-reward reinforcement learning, and proves via matching upper and lower bounds that, for a broad class of environments and at sufficiently high accuracy, learning from a single continuing trajectory is no harder in the worst case than learning with free sampling.
